title: Decide whether commonAuthorityStructure.test.ts should exist at all
description:
Deferred question, raised by the user on 2026-09-22 right after PR #558 merged
(merge commit c3171a28). Not urgent; do not start it as a side quest.

eshyra-4tgd reduced the review-authority guard from 17 tests to 2, each
observing reachability only: CLAUDE.md still carrying the @AGENTS.md import, and
every repository-relative Markdown link in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md resolving.

The open question is whether even those two earn permanent executable status, or
whether the file should be retired entirely. Arguments already on the record, so
a future session need not rederive them:

FOR retention - both failure modes are silent and severe. Losing the import
means sessions stop loading repository authority at all. A dangling pointer
makes an obligation unfollowable. Neither is obvious in a diff.

AGAINST - the whole file is 3 assertions guarding two facts that a broken link
checker, a docs build, or simply opening CLAUDE.md would also reveal, and it is
itself proof machinery under AGENTS.md "Permanent Test Evidence", which says
machinery gets evidence proportionate to the decisions it gates and not an
automatic test. The link guard also needed a fail-open repair within hours of
being written (bc277005), which is weak evidence that the mechanism costs more
to keep correct than the invariant is worth.

If retired, name the replacing responsibility explicitly. Do not replace it with
a new checker, linter config, or CI step - that would move the machinery rather
than dispositioning it.

Related: eshyra-5wbx (beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts, same defect class).
